body: License renewal time. You need 24 hours of continuing education. The online courses are narrated by a robot voice reading a teleprompter about things you already know. The in-person classes are on Saturdays. Your Saturdays are booked through March.

choices.title: Grind the online courses at night
choices.body: Headphones in, modules up, clicking through competence at 11pm.

choices.title: Attend in-person, sacrifice a Saturday
choices.body: Real instruction beats robot narration. Give up the Saturday.

choices.title: Let it slide until the deadline panic
choices.body: Future you can handle it. Present you has pipes to install.

title: Thanksgiving Pipe Burst, Turkey Still Raw
body: Thanksgiving dinner at your sister's. The kitchen sink pipe bursts. Everyone looks at you. You are holding a drumstick. You are wearing a nice shirt. Under the sink is a corroded galvanized fitting from 1978.

choices.title: Fix it in your nice shirt, be a hero
choices.body: This is what you are. Accept it. Save Thanksgiving.

choices.title: Temporary fix, call a plumber Monday
choices.body: Duct tape and a bucket. Proper repair on a non-holiday.

choices.title: Charge your sister a family discount
choices.body: Blood doesn't mean free. Family rate is half price.

title: Food Truck Parks at Your Job Site
body: A food truck figured out that construction sites are full of hungry people with cash. They show up at 11:30 every day with tacos and cold drinks. Productivity drops for 30 minutes. Morale increases for the rest of the day. The foreman is conflicted.

choices.title: Buy the crew lunch, build morale
choices.body: $80 in tacos buys a lot of goodwill.

choices.title: Brown bag it, save the money
choices.body: You have a cooler and a sandwich. The taco truck is a trap.

choices.title: Tell foreman to let people eat in peace
choices.body: Thirty minutes of tacos makes the other seven hours better.

title: You Missed the Turn Thinking About Drains
body: Driving home and you're still mentally rerouting that drain line from this morning. You miss the turn to your street. Your kid is at the door waiting. You realize you've been physically present and mentally absent for weeks.

choices.title: Put the phone on DND after 6pm
choices.body: Work ends when you get home. Enforce it.

choices.title: Accept it, this is the job
choices.body: Plumbers think about plumbing. It's not a 9-to-5.

choices.title: Plan dedicated family evenings
choices.body: Tuesday and Thursday: no work talk. Phone off.

title: Two Crew Members Aren't Speaking
body: Mike and Tony had it out over who left the conduit bender in the rain. It's been three days. They communicate through you like divorced parents. Productivity is down. Tension is up. The conduit bender is fine.

choices.title: Sit them down, mediate like an adult
choices.body: You're not a therapist. But you are the boss.

choices.title: Separate them on different jobs
choices.body: Out of sight, out of mind. Move on.

choices.title: Tell them to figure it out or go home
choices.body: You don't have time for this. Neither does the client.

title: New Truck Day, Finally
body: After 200,000 miles, you're picking up a new work truck. The seats are clean. The radio works. There's no mysterious rattle. You'll ruin it in a month. But right now, driving it off the lot, it smells like possibility and new vinyl.

choices.title: Protect it, install proper tool racks
choices.body: This truck stays organized. New rules. New truck.

choices.title: Drive it to the site, get it dirty
choices.body: Trucks are tools. Tools are for using.

choices.title: Park next to the TikTok plumber's van
choices.body: Let him see what a real work truck looks like.

title: They Offer You Foreman
body: Your foreman blew out his knee on a ladder. Management pulls you aside near the gang box: "You've got the respect of the crew. You can run jobs. We need a foreman by Monday." It's more money, more meetings, and less time on tools. You'd be managing the same guys you were joking with at lunch yesterday.

choices.title: Take the role and own it
choices.body: You take the clipboard and the radio. Everyone congratulates you, then immediately starts blaming you for schedules.

choices.title: Accept a 90-day trial first
choices.body: You say yes, but on trial terms. If it's a bad fit, you walk back to the tools.

choices.title: Pass and stay on the tools
choices.body: You'd rather install pipe than manage personalities. No shame in knowing your lane.

title: Pipe Routing Is Now Classified
body: Data center company slides you an NDA before you can see the building plans. Pipe routing is classified. The security guard checks your toolbox like you're entering a SCIF. You are a plumber. They are treating copper fittings like state secrets. You sign with the hand that was unclogging a toilet four hours ago.

choices.title: Sign it, take the premium rate
choices.body: Classified pipes pay better than declassified ones. Simple math.

choices.title: Walk away from the paranoia
choices.body: You install pipes. If that's a secret, the world has bigger problems.

choices.title: Sign NDA, double the rate
choices.body: If it's secret enough for paperwork, it's secret enough for a premium.

title: Former Google PM Asks About Your Dentist
body: Your union health insurance now covers better doctors than the tech startup PPOs. A former Google PM at your kid's soccer game asks which dentist you use. You tell him. He writes it down. His startup's dental plan covers cleanings and 'wellness consultations,' whatever those are. Yours covers everything. Neither of you says what both of you are thinking.

choices.title: Enjoy the irony quietly
choices.body: Some victories taste better unspoken. This one tastes like fluoride.

choices.title: Post about it online
choices.body: Some things should be said. Loudly. With screenshots of your coverage.

choices.title: Refer him to the union apprenticeship
choices.body: He's got good hands for a desk guy. Maybe.

title: Your Monday Quote Died on Wednesday
body: Bid a commercial refit Monday. Full walkthrough. Measurements. Materials list. Three hours. By Wednesday the architect's AI redesigned the entire HVAC layout. Your quote references rooms that no longer exist. The architect's assistant emails: 'We'll need a revised bid.' She does not apologize for the three hours you spent measuring a building that is now a different building.

choices.title: Rebid fast, don't show frustration
choices.body: Swallow it. Measure again. Bill again. Welcome to the new pace.

choices.title: Add a volatility surcharge
choices.body: All quotes now include a 15% 'redesign insurance' fee. Non-negotiable.

choices.title: Fire the client
choices.body: Your time has a price. Wasting it is not free.

title: Main Street Is Emptying Out
body: Half the storefronts on Main Street are dark. The bookstore. The accountant's office. The travel agency — though that one died years ago. The diner survives on your crew's tabs and data center lunch orders. The barber survives because robots can't do small talk. You're having lunch in a town that's emptying from the inside and your pockets are full of the money that used to circulate here.

choices.title: Buy someone lunch
choices.body: Small gesture. Small cost. Large silence it doesn't fill.

choices.title: Invest in a struggling local business
choices.body: Money goes in. Hope goes in. Math says it won't come back. Do it anyway.

choices.title: Eat your sandwich, mind your business
choices.body: You didn't hollow out Main Street. You just outlasted it.

title: The AI Called You Directly
body: Client's house is managed by an AI system now. It called you when it detected a pressure drop. Texted the exact location, probable cause, and a repair window that fit your calendar. The AI is more polite, more organized, and pays faster than any human client you've ever had. You fixed the pipe in twenty minutes. The homeowner wasn't home. Wasn't notified. Didn't need to be.

choices.title: Take more AI-managed contracts
choices.body: Best client you've ever had doesn't have a pulse. Adjust accordingly.

choices.title: Insist on talking to the homeowner
choices.body: Pipes belong to people. People should know what's happening to their pipes.

choices.title: Set boundaries — humans schedule calls
choices.body: The machine can detect the leak. A person books the appointment.

title: They Want to Tax Your Hands
body: Government proposes a 'critical infrastructure windfall tax' on workers earning over $200K from AI-adjacent industries. Your union is furious. You are doing math. At your current rate, the tax costs $28,000 a year. The op-eds say you're 'benefiting disproportionately from AI infrastructure spending.' You are literally underneath the infrastructure. With a wrench. Disproportionately.

choices.title: Pay it, you can afford it
choices.body: The number hurts. The check clears. Life continues on the right side.

choices.title: Fight it through the union
choices.body: If they want your money, they'll negotiate with 200,000 plumbers first.

choices.title: Hire an accountant, restructure
choices.body: The rich have accountants. You are, apparently, rich.

title: Your Biggest Client Just Evaporated
body: The data center you plumbed for two years. Canceled. Company pivoted to something called 'distributed edge inference.' $180K in outstanding invoices frozen in a bankruptcy filing. Your accountant says 'get in line.' The line has 400 creditors. You are number 312. The boom is still booming everywhere else. But your boom just stopped mid-sentence.

choices.title: Absorb the hit, diversify fast
choices.body: One client was always too many eggs. Expensive lesson. Learned.

choices.title: Lawyer up, fight for your money
choices.body: They owe you for work that exists. Pipes don't un-install themselves.

choices.title: Lean on the union safety net
choices.body: This is what dues are for. The hall has your back. Feels different needing it.

title: The Barbecue Tastes Like Guilt
body: Neighborhood barbecue. Your neighbor Mike lost his accounting job eight months ago. His wife tutors online for $22 an hour. Their kid dropped out of travel soccer. You just bought a new truck. Cash. Mike asks how business is. You say 'good.' You do not say you made more last quarter than he'll make in two years. The burger is excellent. You can barely taste it.

choices.title: Offer Mike work, even odd jobs
choices.body: He can hold a flashlight. That's a start. Dignity has to start somewhere.

choices.title: Keep quiet, guilt is private
choices.body: What do you say? 'Sorry I'm doing well'? There's no good sentence here.

choices.title: Pay for Mike's kid's soccer quietly
choices.body: Anonymous. Through the league office. Mike doesn't need to know.

title: Plumbing Robot v3.0
body: Robot v3. Residential calls. Clean floors. Dry conditions. Good lighting. Handles sixty percent now. You get the rest — the dark, the wet, the old, the weird. Your waitlist is still there. But shorter. Not gone. Shorter. For the first time, the trend line points at you.

choices.title: Specialize deeper into the hard 40%
choices.body: Dark. Wet. Old. Weird. Your moat. Dig it deeper.

choices.title: Invest in the robot company
choices.body: If they're eating your lunch, own the restaurant.

choices.title: Train apprentices for the hard jobs only
choices.body: The easy work is gone. Make sure the hard workers are ready.

title: UBI Passes
body: UBI. Two thousand a month. Your neighbors collect it. They seem fine. Not happy. Not desperate. Fine. You make two thousand before lunch on a Tuesday. The gap doesn't feel like 'hard work' anymore. Doesn't feel like 'lucky hands' either. Something broke. You ended up on the right side. Explaining why is getting harder.

choices.title: Donate the equivalent monthly
choices.body: Match it. Every month. Not guilt. Just... balance.

choices.title: Accept it, this is just how it is
choices.body: You didn't design the system. You just live in it. Like everyone else.

choices.title: Push the union to advocate for higher UBI
choices.body: Two thousand isn't enough. You know what things cost.

title: She Doesn't Want to Fix Things
body: Daughter. Senior year. Wants to study AI. Not plumbing. Not trades. 'The future isn't fixing things, Dad. It's building the things that fix things.' You think she's wrong. You also think she might be right in a way you can't argue with. She has your hands and her mother's brain. She'll be fine. That's not what bothers you.

choices.title: Support her, it's her life
choices.body: Let go. She's not rejecting you. She's continuing you. Differently.

choices.title: Make the case for trades one more time
choices.body: Robots break. Code crashes. Pipes are forever. Say it. Once more.

choices.title: Tell her to do both, you'll pay
choices.body: AI degree and a plumber's license. Belt and suspenders. Your dad's voice.

title: Ron's Replacement Is an Algorithm
body: New building code. AI-generated. 400 pages. Dropped Tuesday. Enforcement Thursday. Ron retired last month. His replacement is an algorithm. It doesn't know your name. Doesn't wave you through. Doesn't have a rental property that needs weekend work. Checks every box. Every single one. Your last three permits took four hours each. Ron's took four minutes.

choices.title: Study the code, comply by Thursday
choices.body: 400 pages. Two nights. Coffee. Compliance. No shortcuts left.

choices.title: Ignore it, dare them to enforce
choices.body: An algorithm can check boxes. It can't check pipe. Come find you.

choices.title: Rally the union for a timeline extension
choices.body: 400 pages in 48 hours is not regulation. It's hazing.

title: A Fifteen-Year-Old Just Halved Your Calls
body: Teenager. Claude. Three weeks. Built a plumbing diagnostic app. Listens to pipes through a phone mic. Identifies problems from sound alone. Can't fix anything. But tells homeowners if they actually need you. Half the time they don't. Your call volume: down 30% in a month. The app is free. She's fifteen. Her operational cost is a laptop and curiosity.

choices.title: Adapt — confirmed-need calls only
choices.body: Fewer calls. Higher value. Every job actually needs you. Adjust.

choices.title: Hire her
choices.body: Can't beat them. Employ them. She could use a mentor.

choices.title: Your hands fix what sound can't diagnose
choices.body: An app hears a rattle. You feel a vibration. Different.

title: Three Data Centers. Same Week. Gone.
body: Three data centers canceled. Same week. 'Edge computing pivot.' No more centralized cooling. No more $800/hr. Tuesday you were booked through next year. Friday you're checking residential leads. The boom didn't end. It relocated. You didn't. Your truck still says 'Data Center Specialist.' The decal cost $400. The irony is free.

choices.title: Pivot to residential, swallow pride
choices.body: Toilets don't pivot. Faucets don't restructure. Back to basics.

choices.title: Chase the next boom
choices.body: Where the data centers go, you go. Pack the truck.

choices.title: You have savings. Take a breath.
choices.body: The panic is real. The savings are also real. Sit. Think. Then move.

title: Your Tax Bill Is a Misprint (It Isn't)
body: Tax bill. Your income tax this year exceeds your total income five years ago. Your accountant laughs. You do not laugh. The IRS does not laugh. You are in a bracket designed for surgeons and hedge fund managers. You are a plumber. Your W-2 looks like a typo. It is not a typo.

choices.title: Pay it, every cent earned
choices.body: The check hurts. The hurt is a privilege. Sign it.

choices.title: Max every deduction, buy the truck
choices.body: Business expense. Depreciation. Mileage. The accountant earns her fee today.

choices.title: Set up the retirement account finally
choices.body: Tax shelter. Future you. Your dad's voice: 'Save it.' Listen this time.
